focus.jtag: After the worst Nasdaq week since April, US futures bounced as the chip selloff lost steam — but VIX is back near 20 with an inverted term structure, oil holds near $100+ on Strait-of-Hormuz disruption, and a wall of megacap earnings (NFLX Tue, META/TSLA/IBM Wed) looms. The full-universe scanner found no qualifying Sniper setup in any of the three types
focus.jnote: The tape is bouncing, but the ground is not stable. US stocks are recovering some ground after last week's rout in chipmakers; Nasdaq 100 contracts climbed 1.1% to snap a weeklong selloff of 5.5% and S&P 500 futures rose 0.4%. A chip-name ETF rallied 3.1% in premarket, set for its first daily gain in 10 sessions. But the week was ugly — the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite recorded their biggest weekly declines since late June on Friday. Volatility is still elevated: VIX rose 21.45% to 19.99 with the term structure in contango at the back but the front-end inverted — VIX1D rose to 23.27, above the 30-day. And oil is the wild card: Brent fell ~1.6% to $108.06 and WTI fell ~0.5% to $100.88, after both settled at multi-month highs Friday. This is a headline-driven, two-sided tape — exactly where a Sniper does not force a trade.
focus.notdown: Energy and the AI-rebound names (chips, megacap tech) are the day's bids — oil-supply fear supports energy, and the dip-buy into earnings lifts semis. The chip ETF's ~3% premarket pop would be its first daily gain in 10 sessions, which is a bounce, not a confirmed trend. These are reflexive, headline-sensitive moves, not clean post-earnings gaps or breakouts — and the scanner confirmed none of them cleared validation. Watch-only; the Type C breakout scan ran (977 examined → 289 within the proximity band → 9 breakout-confirmed → 0 boarded) and nothing held.
focus.notup: Chip/AI shorts are the obvious bear lean after a 5.5% weekly Nasdaq rout — but selling bear calls into a snap-back bounce, with VIX front-end inverted and NFLX/META/TSLA all reporting this week, is a textbook squeeze trap. Last week's damage came from concerns about the cost of financing AI infrastructure, a real risk — but one beat-and-pop from a megacap gaps the whole group up. The Type B news scan pulled 500 headlines → 6 universe tickers with a catalyst → 0 gap-confirmed → 0 boarded. Sell nothing new.
focus.why: Why YELLOW (and why nothing boarded)? Composite ~52 is WARM and P(≥1% gap) ~38% is above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. On top of the gap math, two structural problems: (1) the VIX front-end is inverted (VIX1D > spot), the market's way of pricing near-term event risk; and (2) a wall of megacap earnings — Netflix Tuesday, Meta and Tesla Wednesday — means almost every large-cap has a print inside a normal spread DTE. The scanner ran the full universe and boarded zero in all three types. There is nothing to validate at 9:35. Stand aside; cash is a position.

risks: Megacap earnings wall (this week) — Netflix reports Tuesday 10/20 after the close, with Meta and Tesla both Wednesday 10/21 after the close. Almost every large-cap has a print inside a normal spread DTE — keep every spread clear of its name's earnings date. This is the number-one reason the scan boarded nothing.

Strait of Hormuz / oil — Brent fell ~1.6% to $108.06 and WTI ~0.5% to $100.88 today, after both settled at multi-month highs Friday. Oil near $100+ feeds inflation fear and jet-fuel costs; any fresh incident sends crude vertical — the week's biggest tail.

Inverted VIX front-end — VIX1D rose to 23.27 and sits above the 30-day VIX of 19.99, with the VIX1D/VIX ratio at 1.16. The market is pricing acute near-term event risk; an inverted front-end is a classic stress signal, not a green light to sell premium.

AI-financing fragility (not resolved) — last week's biggest weekly declines since late June were driven by concerns about the cost of financing AI infrastructure. Monday's bounce is a snap-back, not an all-clear — a renewed leg lower could spill from chips into the broad tape.

FOMC Oct 27–28 & Fed blackout — the Fed is in its quiet period from October 17 to 29, with Q3 GDP, September PCE and the Oct 27–28 rate decision set to drive the next move. No Fed-speak this week, so earnings and oil carry the tape — keep any new spread to a DTE that clears both its name's print and the FOMC.
